entry.title: From a Reel Comment to Open Source: Introducing ClipMotion
entry.summary:
While scrolling through Instagram Reels, I came across a website showing animation — a bulb product page where an ON/OFF switch smoothly toggled between images like a crossfade. It looked simple, but the animation was beautifully done. I casually explained how it could be implemented in the comments. That’s when I realized it could be great project since: We constantly get inspired by animations from reels, shorts, and videos But implementing them from scratch every time is repetitive and time-consuming or you might not know to do how do that. What if you could paste a video link and get a reusable animation component? That idea became ClipMotion. ClipMotion is an open-source CLI tool that helps you discover and add animation components inspired by real videos directly into your web projects. ClipMotion is published on npm and works with most package managers. npx clipmotion init
This sets up everything you need. # npx clipmotion <component-name...> npx clipmotion image-crossfade
That’s it. You can think of it as a bridge between animation inspiration and real code. I’ll be honest: I’m not an animation expert. And that’s exactly why ClipMotion is open source. Instead of pretending to know everything, I decided to build a community-driven project. 🎨 Animation requests (Saw a cool animation in a reel? Just link it.) You don’t need to be an animation wizard to contribute. Let’s Build an Animation-Driven Ecosystem If you’ve ever: Saved a reel because of an animation Wanted to recreate it later Or wished animations were easier to reuse Then ClipMotion is for you. 🔗 GitHub: https://github.com/nerdboi008/clipmotion ⭐ Star the repo Sometimes the best projects really do start with a simple comment.

entry.title: AI is moving to the edge – and network security needs to catch up
entry.summary:
Presented by T-Mobile for Business
Small and mid-sized businesses are adopting AI at a pace that would have seemed unrealistic even a few years ago. Smart assistants that greet customers, predictive tools that flag inventory shortages before they happen, and on-site analytics that help staff make decisions faster — these used to be features of the enterprise. Now they’re being deployed in retail storefronts, regional medical clinics, branch offices, and remote operations hubs. What’s changed is not just the AI itself, but where it runs. Presented by SAP
In an era where anyone can spin up an LLM, the real differentiator isn’t the AI technology itself, but the institutional knowledge it’s grounded in. Internal and partner consultants leading operational transformation can’t risk hallucinated guidance when their recommendations impact integrated processes across supply chain, manufacturing, finance, and other core functions.
